description: Five separate corruption effects, each with its own input, output and three controls

params.text: Sets how coarsely the signal is rounded off, 0 to 1; higher settings use fewer and larger voltage steps
Scales its own effect's CV input before that voltage is added to the quantity knob, 0 to 1
Blends between the untouched input and its own effect's processed signal, 0 to 1, starting at half of each
Sets how long each sample is held before a new one is taken, 0 to 1 over a hold of 0 to 32 samples; at 0 the signal passes through untouched
Sets the drive into a tanh waveshaper, 0 to 1 over a gain of 1 to 11
Sets both the chance per sample of starting a stutter and how short the stuttered fragment is, 0 to 1
Sets the chance per sample of dropping the level to a hundredth for a burst of up to a tenth of a second, 0 to 1

inputs.text: The signal fed into the bitcrush effect
The signal fed into the decimate effect
The signal fed into the distort effect
The signal fed into the glitch effect
The signal fed into the crop effect
Added to the bitcrush quantity knob after its attenuator, 10V covering the knob's whole range
Added to the decimate quantity knob after its attenuator, 10V covering the knob's whole range
Added to the distort quantity knob after its attenuator, 10V covering the knob's whole range
Added to the glitch quantity knob after its attenuator, 10V covering the knob's whole range
Added to the crop quantity knob after its attenuator, 10V covering the knob's whole range

outputs.text: Carries the bitcrushed signal blended against the dry input
Carries the decimated signal blended against the dry input
Carries the distorted signal blended against the dry input
Carries the glitched signal blended against the dry input
Carries the cropped signal blended against the dry input

notes: an effect is computed only when both its own input and its own output are patched; leave either one open and that row does nothing
the glitch effect fills a 24000-sample buffer before it starts stuttering, which is half a second at a 48kHz sample rate, and passes the signal through until then
the crop effect drops the level to a hundredth rather than to silence, despite the README describing it as abrupt silencing
the five effects are separate from one another; to chain them, patch one row's output to the next row's input
